name: Trina Vertex S+ 430W
notes: Technology: i-TOPCon cells, dual 1.6mm glass-glass construction, covering two distinct platforms under one series name. Pros: the 144-cell bins (430-455W) run high voltage (Voc 51.4-53.4V) for a wide MPPT startup safety margin, and the glass-glass build gives better long-term durability than a single-glass panel. Cons: the 108-cell bins (500-510W) pack more watts per panel with a much higher current (Isc ~15.9A vs ~10.7A for the 144-cell bins) - check controller Isc limits before choosing a 500W+ bin over the 144-cell range; despite the glass-glass build these panels are wired monofacial, not bifacial, so there's no rear-side yield.

name: Trina Vertex N 700W
notes: Technology: N-Type i-TOPCon cells, 132-cell, bifacial with dual 2.0mm+2.0mm glass (rear pane white-coated). Runs 700-725W - Trina's large-format utility/commercial flagship, distinct from the residential Vertex S+ range and roughly 60% longer. Pros: the highest power and highest efficiency (up to 23.3%) of any panel in Trina's lineup, with the same 12-year product / 30-year linear power warranty (87.4% at year 30) and 10-20% bifacial gain depending on albedo. Cons: at 2384mm and 38.3kg this needs large-format commercial mounting, not standard residential rail or in-roof systems; Isc approaches 18.5A, so check MPPT/tracker current headroom carefully. UK single-unit trade pricing is not yet well established - it is currently sold mainly through factory-direct bulk orders.
